recordedFrom: issue #11170, probe page in Chromium on macOS (reporter's hardware, Korean input source active)
note: The `remapped` case is the reporter's verbatim capture: keydown and keypress both still carry the layout character, and only charCode and the input event's data carry the substituted one. The two negative cases are DERIVED from the same capture by removing the substitution, not separately recorded - see the fixture note on each. No beforeinput record exists in the capture; none is invented here.

cases.name: remapped
cases.note: Verbatim from the issue. ~/Library/KeyBindings/DefaultKeyBinding.dict maps the character the Korean layout puts on Backquote to a backtick. keydown.key is the raw layout character; charCode 96 and input.data carry the OS substitution.

cases.name: no-remap-korean
cases.note: DERIVED, not separately recorded: the `remapped` capture with the dict substitution removed, so the layout's own character is what the text system commits. charCode and input.data become U+20A9 to match keydown.key. This is the paired negative - the same physical key with no remap in play must still deliver the layout character.

cases.name: no-remap-ascii
cases.note: DERIVED, not separately recorded. The issue states that with ABC selected keydown.key is already the backtick and nothing is wrong; this is that sequence. Guards the case where a fix rewrites the Backquote position unconditionally.

cases.name: remapped-neighbour-key
cases.note: DERIVED, not separately recorded. An ordinary letter pressed straight after the remapped key, to catch a fix that leaves the claim armed and swallows or duplicates the next keystroke.
